# 267_R6SEC.2 — ci-anchor honesty (RH-8) + keyed non-prod identity shim (RH-10) + doc (RH-39)

Handoff ticket `267_R6SEC.2` — the two verified findings ordered right after RH-0.

## RH-8 — the required CI check can no longer pass on a red pipeline

`ci-pass anchor` is the ruleset's required check; pre-fix it had `needs:` on all six legs but **no
`if: always()`** — a red leg left the anchor `skipped`, and GitHub counts a skipped required check
as PASSED. Now: `if: always()` on the job + a first gate step (`scripts/ci/assert-needs-green.mjs`,
`NEEDS_JSON: toJSON(needs)`) that fails unless every leg concluded `success`. A
red/skipped/cancelled leg fails the check. The `mode == 'full'` upload gates are intact — fast
runs still never write anchors.

## RH-10 — non-prod header identity is keyed, not forgeable

Non-prod api services are publicly reachable (`allUsers` invoker + `INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL`), and the
shim trusted three client-forgeable `x-rhema-*` headers verbatim. Now the api resolves header
identity **only** when the request also presents the stage's shared key on `x-rhema-identity-key`:

- Pulumi mints `rhema-<stage>-identity-headers-key` per non-prod stage (`random.RandomPassword`
  SecretVersion; api SA `secretAccessor`; api env carries the secret's NAME — never the value).
  `identity-headers-key` stays out of `ALL_SECRET_IDS` (the `system-database-url` precedent) —
  **prod's provisioned set, IAM, and env are untouched**; the shim was never armed there.
- `IDENTITY_HEADERS=true` with no resolvable key fails **closed** (shim off + boot log).
- Callers audited and plumbed: `LiveWorkflowLauncher` → `identityKey` header; `run-live-exit`
  (`RHEMA_IDENTITY_KEY`); `res1-probe`/`research-probe-live` (`PROBE_IDENTITY_KEY`); the web
  forwarder relays the 4th header. `cite1-leg` (cookie-only), journeys preview legs (real
  sessions), and the local stub-api test are unaffected.
- Constant-time key compare; missing/wrong key yields the same `null` — no oracle.

## RH-39 — `apps/api/AGENTS.md` gotcha 4 rewritten

The unkeyed fallback is no longer described as acceptable; the doc now states the keyed invariant
(never re-enable the unkeyed shim). `docs/ci.md`'s anchor row updated for the new behavior.
